The Hottest DJs of 2026: Our Top 5 Men and Top 5 Women

By PLURGASM @plurgasm ⏱ 6 min read

This is an opinion piece, and a fun one. "Hottest" here means two things at once: who has the most heat in 2026 (stadium shows, sold-out runs, surprise albums) and who brings the most presence and style to the booth. We ranked five men and five women. You will disagree with us, and that is the point.

In This List

  • How We Ranked Them
  • Top 5 Men
  • Top 5 Women
  • Who Did We Miss?

How We Ranked Them

  • The buzz: big 2026 moments like headline debuts, arena tours, new albums and festival slots.
  • The presence: how much energy they put into a room. You know it when you see it.
  • The style: the look, the swagger, the whole package.

Every fact below is sourced. The rankings are pure PLURGASM opinion.

Top 5 Men

1. Dom Dolla

Nobody had a bigger year at home. Dom Dolla headlined Melbourne's Marvel Stadium on September 24, a homecoming that followed his sold-out Allianz Stadium debut in Sydney in December 2025[1]. Next up is his biggest standalone headline show yet, at Auckland Domain in New Zealand on February 6, 2027[2].

Why he's #1: stadium-level fame, and he still plays like he is in a sweaty club. Easy pick.

2. John Summit

John Summit went all in on 2026 with his album CTRL ESCAPE and a North American arena tour of the same name, running October 1 to December 4 with stops at TD Garden, United Center and Barclays Center[3]. He also played Kinetic Field at EDC Las Vegas in May[4].

Why he's here: the everyman-turned-arena-headliner story, plus a crowd that sings every word back to him.

3. Mau P

Mau P just announced his first arena tour behind his debut album, Generation Rebrand, due in spring 2027. It includes an open-to-close set at BMO Stadium in Los Angeles in January 2027 and a March 6 headline show at Madison Square Garden, which EDM Identity reports is the first single-headliner show for a dance music act at the venue[5].

Why he's here: tech house's biggest glow-up. Same guy who made big room bangers as Maurice West, now headlining the Garden.

4. Sammy Virji

Sammy Virji surprise-dropped his third album, Open Late, on October 21, revealing it at a pop-up party at 93 Feet East in London[6]. Days earlier he headlined Red Rocks on October 16, with Confidence Man (DJ set), Oppidan and Sam Alfred in support[7].

Why he's here: UK garage's main character. Effortlessly cool, and he makes it look easy.

5. KETTAMA

KETTAMA played Circuit Grounds at EDC Las Vegas in May[4], and he closes the year in one of the biggest house sets on the calendar: a b3b with Cloonee and Josh Baker at Proper NYE / NYD in San Diego[8]. See every New Year's festival in our December 2026 raves guide.

Why he's here: Relentless energy and that grin behind the decks. The b3b sets alone earn him a spot.

Top 5 Women

1. Sara Landry

The Austin-based hard techno queen made her long-awaited Red Rocks debut on October 10, sharing the bill with Pendulum, Supergloss and Lorely Mur[9]. She is also on the Proper NYE / NYD bill in San Diego to close out the year[8].

Why she's #1: nobody owns a stage like she does. Dark, fast and impossible to look away from.

2. Peggy Gou

Peggy Gou, the Incheon-born DJ behind "(It Goes Like) Nanana," headlined the Saturday night concert at LIV Golf Korea in Busan on May 30[10]. She also played Neon Garden at EDC Las Vegas, including a b2b with KI/KI[4].

Why she's here: she was dubbed the "world's hippest DJ" for a reason[11]. A real fashion icon, and her sets are still a party.

3. Indira Paganotto

The Spanish DJ, born in the Canary Islands and raised in Madrid, runs her own label, Artcore, and has collaborated with Armin van Buuren on "Dragon"[12]. In 2026 she brought her psychedelic, trance-tinged techno to Neon Garden at EDC Las Vegas[4].

Why she's here: pure fire energy behind the decks. When she plays, the whole crowd locks in.

4. Mary Droppinz

Mary Droppinz had a stacked 2026. Her festival run included Okeechobee, EDC Las Vegas, Project Glow, Electric Forest, HARD Summer, North Coast, EDC Korea and III Points[13], including a Basspod set at EDC[4]. She is also booked for Jackpot in Las Vegas and HiJinx in Philadelphia this December[14].

Why she's here: bass music's hardest-working woman, and she always looks like she is having the time of her life.

5. Alyssa Jolee

Repping Long Beach, Alyssa Jolee is one of the names most tied to West Coast hard techno right now[15]. She played the Wasteland stage at EDC Las Vegas in May[4], and she is booked for Toxic Winter in San Francisco on February 5 and 6, 2027[15]. Follow her at @alyssajmo.

Why she's here: our rising-star pick. Big style, harder kicks, and a SoCal following that keeps growing.

Who Did We Miss?

This list is all love and all opinion. Every DJ here earned their spot with the music first. Think we got it wrong? Tell us who belongs on the list at @PlurgasmHQ or beastmodebass7@gmail.com.

Want to see them live? Check the 2027 rave schedule for every festival by month, or find out what genre your favorite bass artist plays in our bass artist genre directory.
